interactions.summary: Sneako says Malaysian contacts, including the Prince of Johor, are already talking about education reform, and Jiang answers that his hoped-for school would function as a lab school where educators can observe new practices and adapt them back home.

Sneako says he wants to be a student in Jiang's coming livestream series, and Jiang answers with concrete details about a two-week June class at the Yale Beijing Center that will also be livestreamed globally for anyone who wants to read Dante line by line.

Sneako asks what Dante's Inferno has to do with Jiang's larger concerns, and Jiang answers that the Divine Comedy is a full spiritual journey from hell through purgatory to paradise, where one must confront suffering and evil before appreciating the good and the divine.

speaker_notes.note: Jiang's June seminar description is concrete enough to matter chronologically: it names the mid-June to end-June window, Yale Beijing Center, an in-person cohort, and a parallel public livestream. Those implementation details should not be flattened into a generic future teaching plan.
Sneako's line about 'Frankism' and the monad is a playful recap, not Jiang's own formal terminology. Preserve it as conversational texture rather than a durable Jiang-authored concept.

claims.claim: Jiang says his envisioned school in Malaysia would function as a lab school where local educators can observe separate practices and adapt them back into their own systems.
He says the Dante seminar is scheduled for mid-to-late June 2026 at the Yale Beijing Center, with a small in-person cohort and a global livestream for broader participation.
claims.temporal_scope: Planned June 2026 teaching event stated on 2026-05-18.

claims.claim: Jiang says the seminar is aimed at students interested in liberal arts and humanities teaching, but the main point is to let anyone in the world read the Divine Comedy line by line alongside him.
claims.temporal_scope: Teaching purpose stated on 2026-05-18 about a planned June 2026 event.

claims.claim: He says the Divine Comedy should leave readers empowered to confront the text for themselves because the work is meant to initiate a spiritual journey through life.
claims.temporal_scope: Interpretive and pedagogical claim stated on 2026-05-18.

claims.claim: Jiang defines the Divine Comedy as a spiritual journey through hell, purgatory, and paradise in which enlightenment requires prior confrontation with suffering, sin, and evil.

signature_moments.moment: The future school is imagined not as a private enclave but as a demonstrator site where educators can witness a different practice and carry pieces of it back into their own institutions.
signature_moments.source_phrase: this school will be a lab school
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It gives Jiang's Malaysia ambition a concrete educational mechanism rather than leaving it as vague community talk.

signature_moments.moment: A small Beijing seminar becomes a world-facing Dante classroom, reading line by line so anyone anywhere can finally enter the book.
signature_moments.source_phrase: we'll livestream it to the world
signature_moments.why_it_matters: This is the packet's clearest fusion of elite intellectual setting and mass public pedagogy.

signature_moments.moment: Dante's path is reduced to one hard rule: if you want enlightenment, you first have to go through hell and learn what evil really is.
signature_moments.source_phrase: you first have to experience hell
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It connects Jiang's literary teaching to his broader worldview that suffering is a necessary stage of transformation.

glossary_terms.definition_or_usage: Jiang's proposed educational site where teachers can observe new practices directly and carry them back into the wider Malaysian system.
Jiang's framing of the Divine Comedy as a path through suffering, sin, and evil toward divine encounter and enlightenment.

chronology_notes.note: The packet moves from Malaysia-specific education-reform opportunity, to concrete June 2026 seminar planning in Beijing, to Jiang's core interpretive frame for why Dante matters: spiritual ascent depends on first confronting hell, suffering, and evil.

uncertainty_notes.note: This packet mixes dated logistical plans with Jiang's literary interpretation of Dante. Downstream work should preserve both layers separately rather than treating the interpretive account as proof that the seminar or school project will unfold exactly as hoped.
